text:
Asha (eng-platform): Heads-up — putting a very small RFC follow-up on the surgical canary idea. Trying to sketch a decoupled fallback interface that avoids routing-layer state bloat. Quick thoughts?

Riley (eng-runtime): +1 to keeping routing stateless. how are you thinking about detection signals vs decision authority?

Asha (eng-platform): thinking: router provides signals (latency P95, error spike, model-quality regressions) and a separate canary-decider service owns the policy + short-lived leases. router subscribes to decisions, not internal candidate state.

Noah (eng-infra): That reduces per-router memory, but adds network hops. Are we okay with the added RPC on the fast path?

Asha (eng-platform): Router path is still local fast-path for accepted requests. The decision sync is asynchronous with a tiny cached copy + TTL. On anomaly, routers consult decider sync and can trigger immediate short-circuit. The extra hop is mainly on policy changes, not every request.

Dee (product): Clarify: product wants canaries to auto-flip back on quality regressions (not just errors). We need an API for injecting eval scores into the decision surface.

Riley (eng-runtime): +1. Suggest we standardize signal names: latency_ms_p95, err_rate_5m, eval_score_rolling. decider can accept weighted rules.

Noah (eng-infra): Failure modes: decider unavailable, stale decisions, split-brain between replicas. Can we make routers have a clear fallback behavior: prefer last-known decision, then global safe-mode if TTL expired?

Asha (eng-platform): Exactly. Proposal: TTL-based decision cache on routers. If TTL expired -> consult fallback policy (policy tiers: allowlist -> degrade -> block). Also expose a per-tenant emergency override for ops.

ops-oncall: If we implement TTL + emergency override, please add an audit log event and a one-click revert in console. We live in the revert button. :grin:

deploy-bot: deploy started for canary-decider v0.3 -> 3/5 hosts. ETA 6m.

Riley (eng-runtime): A quick config sketch (pseudo):
```json
{
  "canary_policy": {
    "name": "surgical-v1",
    "signals": ["latency_ms_p95","err_rate_5m","eval_score_rolling"],
    "thresholds": {
      "latency_ms_p95": 350,
      "err_rate_5m": 0.02,
      "eval_score_rolling": 0.88
    },
    "decisions": {
      "pass": "route",
      "warn": "reduce_traffic",
      "fail": "fallback_model"
    },
    "decision_ttl_seconds": 15
  }
}
```

Dee (product): Good. Also include a small traffic-sample window for evaluation (e.g., 500 requests) so eval scores aren't noisy.

Noah (eng-infra): Ops / SRE note: add circuit-breaker counters to the decider telemetry, and instrument decision propagation latency. If propagation > X, routers should assume degraded and apply conservative policies.

Asha (eng-platform): Implementation notes:
- decider publishes diffs to a pubsub + exposes a read API for on-demand checks
- routers keep a tiny LRU cache keyed by (tenant, route) of last decision + expiry
- fallback policies are hierarchical: global safe-mode -> tenant override -> route-specific rule

Riley (eng-runtime): Can we avoid per-tenant explosion? maybe default inherit from model-catalog tags and only materialize exceptions.

Asha (eng-platform): yes — defaulting is key. We'll only create explicit rules when a customer requests canary or ops triggers. Everything else uses catalog defaults.

ops-oncall: one more ask: include a read-only /health endpoint on decider that returns "fresh" if >75% routers report up-to-date decisions. Helps incident runs.

Noah (eng-infra): Agree. Also: plan a degraded-path test in chaos week to simulate decider outage and TTL expiry.

Asha (eng-platform): I'll draft a short RFC with diagrams and a minimal API spec. Goal: ship a beta in 3 sprints. Thanks all — ping me if you want a slot on the design doc. :rocket:
